pr_title: Change Dynamic header underlying data type from byte[] to string
pr_body:
# Perf results:

## Dynamic table
Insertion into dynamic table:

### Before:

| Method |     Mean |     Error |    StdDev | Gen 0 | Gen 1 | Gen 2 | Allocated |
|------- |---------:|----------:|----------:|------:|------:|------:|----------:|
| Insert | **1.459 us** | 0.0700 us | 0.1974 us |     - |     - |     - |      **88 B** |

### After:

| Method |     Mean |    Error |   StdDev | Gen 0 | Gen 1 | Gen 2 | Allocated |
|------- |---------:|---------:|---------:|------:|------:|------:|----------:|
| Insert | **234.7 ns** | 12.73 ns | 37.35 ns |     - |     - |     - |      **48 B** |

## HeaderField constructor

There was removed the main allocation issue

### Before:
| Method |     Mean |   Error |  StdDev |  Gen 0 | Gen 1 | Gen 2 | Allocated |
|------- |---------:|--------:|--------:|-------:|------:|------:|----------:|
|    Ctr | **336.0 ns** | 6.66 ns | 7.13 ns | 0.1121 |     - |     - |     **704 B** |
### After:
| Method |     Mean |    Error |   StdDev | Gen 0 | Gen 1 | Gen 2 | Allocated |
|------- |---------:|---------:|---------:|------:|------:|------:|----------:|
|    Ctr | **21.86 ns** | 0.107 ns | 0.101 ns |     - |     - |     - |         **-** |

##HeaderDescriptor

I added new string overload for *GetHeaderValue* method as the original with byte[] is used by HTTP2 and there was a performance penalty to convert the value to string before.

As you can see there is a significant performance hit for Location headers, however, this path is not used in HTTP2. I would like to discuss this in the PR.

### Before:
|                             Method |      Mean |    Error |   StdDev |  Gen 0 | Gen 1 | Gen 2 | Allocated |
|----------------------------------- |----------:|---------:|---------:|-------:|------:|------:|----------:|
|       GetHeaderValue_Bytes_Unknown |  **34.96 ns** | 0.355 ns | 0.315 ns | 0.0114 |     - |     - |      **72 B** |
|         GetHeaderValue_Bytes_Known |  **46.35 ns** | 0.296 ns | 0.247 ns | 0.0114 |     - |     - |      **72 B** |
|      GetHeaderValue_Bytes_Location |  **87.41 ns** | 0.995 ns | 0.931 ns | 0.0114 |     - |     - |      **!!** *72 B* |
| GetHeaderValue_Bytes_Location_utf8 | **109.67 ns** | 2.222 ns | 5.366 ns | 0.0114 |     - |     - |  **!!**    *72 B* |
### After:
|                              Method |       Mean |     Error |    StdDev |  Gen 0 | Gen 1 | Gen 2 | Allocated |
|------------------------------------ |-----------:|----------:|----------:|-------:|------:|------:|----------:|
|       GetHeaderValue_String_Unknown |   **3.719 ns** | 0.0983 ns | 0.1009 ns |      - |     - |     - |         **-** |
|         GetHeaderValue_String_Known |   **4.268 ns** | 0.0332 ns | 0.0294 ns |      - |     - |     - |         **-** |
|      GetHeaderValue_String_Location | **!! 208.229 ns** | 3.1741 ns | 2.8138 ns | 0.0203 |     - |     - |     **!!**    *128 B* |
| GetHeaderValue_String_Location_utf8 | **!! 242.598 ns** | 2.5850 ns | 2.2916 ns | 0.0200 |     - |     - |     **!!**    *128 B* |

## HpackDecoder

It is visible that the decoder doesn't allocate in case of dynamic/static headers at all

### Before:

|                                 Method |     Mean |    Error |   StdDev |  Gen 0 | Gen 1 | Gen 2 | Allocated |
|--------------------------------------- |---------:|---------:|---------:|-------:|------:|------:|----------:|
| DecodesIndexedHeaderField_DynamicTable | **81.19 ns** | 1.149 ns | 1.075 ns | 0.0153 |     - |     - |      **96 B **|
|  DecodesIndexedHeaderField_StaticTable | **76.35 ns** | 1.746 ns | 2.331 ns | 0.0114 |     - |     - |      **72 B** |

### After:

|                                 Method |     Mean |    Error |   StdDev |   Median | Gen 0 | Gen 1 | Gen 2 | Allocated |
|--------------------------------------- |---------:|---------:|---------:|---------:|------:|------:|------:|----------:|
| DecodesIndexedHeaderField_DynamicTable | **14.61 ns** | 0.501 ns | 0.419 ns | 14.45 ns |     - |     - |     - |         **-** |
|  DecodesIndexedHeaderField_StaticTable | **13.42 ns** | 0.313 ns | 0.808 ns | 13.10 ns |     - |     - |     - |         **-** |

## Http client

The main improvement is in simple get with an empty body (*Get*) as Kestrel sends value from the static table. Another requests with custom headers are equal as this change is not related to encoding (*GetWithHeaders*) and the Kestrel don't send dynamic headers in the response (*GetWithHeaders_Echo*)

### Before:

|              Method |     Mean |    Error |   StdDev |  Gen 0 | Gen 1 | Gen 2 | Allocated |
|-------------------- |---------:|---------:|---------:|-------:|------:|------:|----------:|
|                 Get | **449.6 us** | 10.03 us | 28.13 us | 0.4883 |     - |     - |   **4.58 KB** |
|      GetWithHeaders | 467.2 us | 10.36 us | 30.55 us |      - |     - |     - |   5.11 KB |
| GetWithHeaders_Echo | 469.3 us |  9.25 us | 13.84 us | 0.9766 |     - |     - |   6.53 KB |

### After:

|              Method |     Mean |   Error |   StdDev |  Gen 0 | Gen 1 | Gen 2 | Allocated |
|-------------------- |---------:|--------:|---------:|-------:|------:|------:|----------:|
|                 Get | **344.2 us** | 7.69 us |  9.44 us | 0.4883 |     - |     - |   **3.76 KB** |
|      GetWithHeaders | 431.6 us | 8.55 us |  9.50 us | 0.4883 |     - |     - |   5.12 KB |
| GetWithHeaders_Echo | 468.8 us | 9.19 us | 12.58 us | 0.9766 |     - |     - |   6.53 KB |

Fixes #31861

issue_context.title: [HTTP/2] Change headers type in HPack tables from byte[] to string
issue_context.body: This change should avoid unnecessary string -> byte[] conversion and allocation. When Hpack decrypts table values it just returns the string without any conversion.
comments:
There is obvious improvement in simple GET requests (see the #31864 for details). The improvement is on .NET Core and I expect the same benefit on the Kestrel side as the code is shared. There are two concerns:
* AspNet team -  how it is aligned with dotnet/aspnetcore#17400
* @scalablecory - performance trade: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/31864#discussion_r375986160

review_comments:
I don't know that this is the way we should do this. You're trading performance here: dynamic headers that get reused will be cheaper now, but non-dynamic headers, or ones that don't get reused, will become more expensive.

HttpClient keeps its own interned strings around (the KnownHeader + known values table), so for many common headers it will not allocate any new strings. This change would instead allocate a string for every new header it sees.

A better solution might be to move the `KnownHeader` table into shared code and have `HPackEncoder` directly map to it when possible or allocate new strings if not. This would depend heavily on if Kestrel could make use of such a table. With some small changes this could also clean up a layering concern @Tratcher had re: exposing static indexes as an optimization.

Maybe it can be solved together with https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/17400 as a plugin byte decoder. We can use our Known header optimizations in Libraries and Kestrel would use their own.
If I'm not wrong this can introduce memory corruption in case we return dynamic value which is deleted later. What is your opinion?

It won't introduce memory corruption, but you could end up pointing to stale or different header data.  So, not something that should be done unless there's a guarantee I'm not seeing that the referenced slot will remain containing the same data indefinitely.
this path is not accessible from HTTP2 and for HTTP1.1 there is an original method. I was about to remove this branch

I'm struggling to understand the change.

I get that this is saving a string => byte[] conversion for the static table, but that's a one-time startup thing and could be addressed in other ways.

I get that we were previously converting the span name/value to byte[] in HeaderField, which is something I commented on in the original PR.  But there are different ways to address that, basically just making sure that the callers of this ctor are passing in logically immutable byte[]s.

Storing byte[] is in general going to result in storing half as much memory for these headers, and we're reading bytes from the wire and writing bytes to the wire, so using byte[] seems like it should actually be a better format that would avoid transcoding costs.

What am I missing?
This change is targeting the dynamic table decoder: rather than have HttpClient/Kestrel allocate new strings based on byte arrays, they are allocated just once and then reused.
Why would they allocate strings at all?
Oh, e.g. to hand out as part of the HttpClient response header collection?
